findings: Reviewed 0.2.8 (head c5cc01a) against 0.2.7 with scratch clones under the scratchpad. The stamp change is a seamless upgrade: 0.2.7 already wrote an ISO time plus newline into .git/locker-fetched, so an old file is read as is (tried with its mtime set to 2020: no fetch, age 0). Trailing spaces, CRLF and a blank line parse; an empty file, garbage, nulls, a bare epoch number and a date with no time all give null and the command fetches and rewrites the stamp; a stamp 2 s in the future fetches, 2 s in the past does not. A directory at that path crashes with EISDIR on the write, the same as main, so not new. The new test passed three times out of three in node --test (5.42 s each, 22 of 22, the process exits in about 31 s, no timer kept alive since the 3300 ms timer is awaited). It does prove the folder comes back: with 0.2.6's finally condition (was !== slice) put into a scratch copy, the test fails with actual main, expected slice/g. npm test 28 pass on the new head, npm run lines 1105, no em dash in the diff, 0.2.8 in package.json, package-lock.json and mcp.js, and DESIGN and the backlog say what the code does. The first pass of this review found the README's Not in the suite sentence had dropped LEASE_NOT_MINE, which no test asserts, and listed PUSH_REFUSED while test line 384 asserts backup's; c5cc01a fixes both and the sentence now matches the suite. Polish, no change needed: the 0.05 minute lease gives the two accept calls before the gate 3 s to finish, ample here but the margin to watch on a slow box.
